candidate.attacker: A signed-in user who owns any business and knows a scheduled shift UUID in a different business. A non-admin employee in the victim business can discover published shift IDs and create their own business through createBusiness.
candidate.counterevidence: Server services correctly scope their own writes and queries; they do not protect direct Data API writes. Existing location unique keys prevent poisoning an already-created shift location, so target a scheduled shift without a location. The attack needs a real shift UUID; published schedule discovery gives it to ordinary eligible employees.
candidate.impact: Cross-tenant integrity corruption and persistent denial of starting a victim shift, including offline preparation/start workflows. The victim cannot remove the poisoning row through its tenant-scoped UI. Similar global pair uniqueness with unscoped FKs exists for shift_assignments and product_recipe_items.
candidate.invariant: Every relational reference in a tenant row must point to an object in the same business; ownership of one tenant must not affect another tenant's workflow.
candidate.remediation: Remove authenticated setup DML grants if setup must run only through server services, or enforce same-business composite FKs and equivalent RLS checks on every writable relationship. Cover INSERT and UPDATE and clean existing invalid cross-tenant rows before applying constraints. Regression test owner-of-A direct writes targeting shift B plus successful start of B.
source_evidence: RLS WITH CHECK contains only exists business_members where bm.business_id = inventory_locations.business_id and bm.auth_user_id = auth.uid() and bm.role in ('owner','admin').
Server start lookup requires inventoryLocations.businessId = access.business.id, but the subsequent insert must satisfy the global shiftId unique.
source_to_sink: Supabase REST authenticated INSERT/UPDATE public.inventory_locations accepts attacker-controlled business_id and shift_id.
Data API grant permits the write; RLS checks owner/admin membership for row.business_id only.
shift_id references public.shifts(id) without business_id, so the database accepts a foreign-tenant shift.
The global unique inventory_locations_shift_id_unique reserves the victim shift ID.
Victim startAssignedShift searches for a same-business location, sees none, and its legitimate INSERT fails against the attacker-created unique key.
candidate.title: Data API setup writes can attach another tenant's shift and block its start

candidate.attacker: Any network client able to POST to the web app; it can set Origin to the request origin without an authenticated session.
candidate.counterevidence: Browser-origin CSRF protection exists, and services reject unauthorized uploads and oversized selected files. Those checks occur after materialization. A deployment proxy might cap request sizes but no such production limit is established in repository configuration. The JSON offline endpoints already enforce a streaming 1 MB limit.
candidate.impact: Oversized multipart requests, including extra parts, can consume the Node process's memory and CPU before rejection, denying service to normal requests.
candidate.invariant: Untrusted request bodies must be bounded before parsing and large uploads should not be consumed before authorization.
candidate.remediation: Authenticate before consuming the body and enforce a total streaming request-byte limit before formData parsing, independent of Content-Length; bound all parts, not just the selected file. Return 413 on excess and cancel the stream. Add a bounded route test for chunked oversized and extra-part requests.
source_evidence: The 3.5 MB file guard lives inside the downstream service, after formData has already consumed the body.
next.config.ts sets experimental.serverActions.bodySizeLimit only; the vulnerable endpoint is an App Router route handler.
source_to_sink: POST /api/offline/proof checks Origin but does not authenticate.
It calls await request.formData() with no byte limit, reading/materializing the entire body and every submitted part.
Only after parsing does attachPaymentProof or attachDiscountProof call requireActiveBusiness and enforce the individual file-size limit.
candidate.title: Unauthenticated proof requests parse an unbounded multipart body

candidate.attacker: An unauthenticated registrant who knows an invited email address and can submit registration for it.
candidate.counterevidence: requireUser later validates the Auth session, so an unconfirmed account with no session cannot immediately use normal protected routes. The local config does not explicitly establish hosted email-confirmation policy. Auth provider behavior on duplicate registrations also limits some attack variants; no duplicate-account takeover is asserted.
candidate.impact: An unverified registration consumes pending business invitations, including admin invitations, and creates active tenant authorization records before identity verification. Whether the registrant can immediately use that membership depends on Auth email-confirmation/session policy; the source alone does not prove an immediately authenticated account takeover.
candidate.invariant: Email-address invitations may become active memberships only after the account has proved ownership of that email address.
candidate.remediation: Make verified email ownership a guard inside claimMembershipInvitations and avoid activating invitations from an unconfirmed signUp response. Claim only after a verified callback/login/current-user result. Test that an unconfirmed signup leaves invitations pending and a confirmed user claims exactly once.

claimMembershipInvitations reads user.email and has no email_confirmed_at check.

candidate.attacker: Remote unauthenticated HTTP client able to set Origin equal to the application origin and send arbitrary multipart bodies.
counterevidence: Individual proof services enforce authentication, assignment, 3.5 MB size and signature checks, but all occur after multipart parsing.
The repository configures a 4mb Server Actions limit; this route is a Route Handler.
No repository deployment ingress policy was found. A platform-enforced request body cap could limit practical memory amplification.
No application or network exploit was executed; this is source-based validation.
candidate.flow: POST /api/offline/proof → assertSameOrigin (header equality only) → request.formData() reads/parses the entire supplied multipart body → attachPaymentProof/attachDiscountProof → requireActiveBusiness and per-file size validation.
candidate.impact: A self-hosted or otherwise uncapped deployment can expend large memory/CPU parsing oversized multipart data before rejecting authentication or file size, degrading request availability. Effective external ingress limits may reduce impact.
candidate.invariant: An unauthenticated request must not cause application memory and parsing work proportional to an unbounded body; accepted proof payloads are limited to 3.5 MB.
candidate.remediation: Authenticate POS access before consuming the body and bound total bytes read from request.body, including chunked requests and multipart overhead, before constructing/parsing FormData. Do not rely only on Content-Length. Preserve existing per-file signature/size checks.
